title: The Story of Saint Joseph
summary: Joseph cares for Mary and Jesus through journeys, hard decisions and everyday family life.
coverAlt: Imaginative illustration of Joseph with Mary and Jesus in an imaginative family scene

pages.title: Joseph of Nazareth
pages.body: Around the beginning of the first century, Joseph lived in Nazareth in Galilee. He was a carpenter, working with his hands. He was promised in marriage to Mary. Then he learned that she was expecting a child. Matthew's Gospel calls Joseph a just man. He did not want to expose Mary to public shame, but he had a difficult decision before him.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: Welcoming Mary
pages.body: In a dream, an angel told Joseph not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife. Her child was from the Holy Spirit. The angel told him to name the baby Jesus. When Joseph woke, he did what the angel had asked. He welcomed Mary as his wife. Caring for her and the child became part of the life he would share with them.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: The Journey to Bethlehem
pages.body: Joseph and Mary traveled from Nazareth to Bethlehem. Luke's Gospel tells us that Jesus was born there. Mary wrapped him and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place. A manger was a feeding trough, not a grand cradle. In this simple place, Mary and Joseph cared for the child Christians call God's Son.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: A Name and a Family
pages.body: Joseph gave the baby the name Jesus, as the angel had told him. He was not Jesus' biological father, but he accepted the responsibility of being his earthly father and guardian. The family's life had begun with a journey and a birth far from Nazareth. Now another journey would ask Joseph to act quickly to keep the child safe.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: Seeking Safety in Egypt
pages.body: An angel warned Joseph in a dream that Herod wanted to harm Jesus. Joseph rose, took Mary and the child during the night, and left for Egypt. They stayed there while Herod was alive. Leaving meant becoming a family far from home, but it took the child away from danger. Joseph's care for Jesus now meant finding safety in another land.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: Returning to Nazareth
pages.body: After Herod died, an angel again appeared to Joseph in a dream. Joseph brought Mary and Jesus back. But he learned that Herod's son was ruling in Judea, and he was afraid to go there. Warned in another dream, he went to Galilee. The family settled in Nazareth. The journeys had brought them to the town where Jesus would grow up.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: Work and Growing Together
pages.body: In Nazareth, Jesus grew in the care of Mary and Joseph. Joseph was known as a carpenter, and Jesus as the carpenter's son. Their family life belonged to this small town. There was work to do, and the child was growing. The family also traveled together for worship. Each year, Mary and Joseph went to Jerusalem for the Passover festival.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: The Search in Jerusalem
pages.body: When Jesus was twelve, they took him to Jerusalem for Passover. On the way home, Mary and Joseph realized he was not with their traveling group. They searched among relatives and friends, then returned to Jerusalem. After three days, they found him in the Temple. He was listening to the teachers and asking questions. Mary told him how worried they had been. If you are separated from your caregivers, ask a safe, trusted adult for help.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: Faithful Care
pages.body: Jesus returned with Mary and Joseph to Nazareth and was obedient to them. He grew in wisdom and age. Joseph's care had carried the family through a birth, danger, journeys, and a search for their missing child. At home again, their daily life continued. Christians remember Joseph for this faithful care. The carpenter of Nazareth had made a home for Jesus and stayed beside him as he grew.

evidence.claim: Original imaginative composite illustration, not a documentary reconstruction.

pages.title: Points of reflection
pages.body:
Joseph's care sometimes meant leaving home and sometimes returning to ordinary work. Which moment in his story shows you something about caring for a family? Talk about it together.

Read Luke, chapter two, verses fifty-one and fifty-two with someone who cares for you. Jesus returns to Nazareth with Mary and Joseph, and grows in wisdom and age. This passage brings us back to their life at home.

Try one useful kindness at home today. You could put something away or help with a task that fits your age.

God, thank you for the people who care for me. Help me notice when someone needs kindness, and give me the courage to ask for help. Saint Joseph, pray for us. Amen.
